sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Startup, fonts, styles and mounting
sections.what: Loads the fonts and global styles, checks that the page has the root element, then draws the app inside StrictMode.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping global setup in one startup file makes it easy to find.
sections.watch_out: The explicit root check gives a clearer error than the default failure when the element is missing.

summary: The entry point of the frontend. It loads fonts and global styles, finds the page element with the id root, and starts the app inside React's StrictMode.
why: Likely reason: this is the standard place to start a React app. StrictMode is a development setting that flags unsafe code.
how: First it loads the variable and serif fonts and the global stylesheet. Then it finds the root element. If the element is missing, it stops with a clear error. Otherwise it renders the App component inside StrictMode.
inputs: The page element with the id root in the HTML file, plus the font and style packages.
outputs: The rendered application in the browser.
risks: If the root element is missing, the app will not start. StrictMode runs effects twice in development, so setup code must clean up properly.
debug: If the page is blank, check the browser console for the root error. If fonts look wrong, check the font imports. If effects seem to run twice, that is expected in development under StrictMode.
